46927-life-and-marvelous-adventures-of-w.title: And Spy America Ever Produced.
46927-life-and-marvelous-adventures-of-w.creator: J. W. Buel,
46927-life-and-marvelous-adventures-of-w.description: A book by J. W. Buel,. stands alone, without a prototype; his originality is as conspicuous as his remarkable escapades. He was desperate without being a desperado; a fighter without that disposition which invites danger or craves the excitement of an encounter. He killed many men, but in every instance it was either in self-defense or in the prosecution of a duty which he deemed justifiable.

arxiv-2004-04132.title: The Gaia Ultra-Cool Dwarf Sample – III: Seven new multiple systems containing at least one Gaia DR2 ultra-cool dwarf. 2020 The Gaia Ultra-Cool Dwarf Sample – III: Seven new multiple systems containing at least one Gaia DR2 ultra-cool dwarf. – 6
arxiv-2004-04132.creator: F. Marocco, R. L. Smart, E. E. Mamajek, L. M. Sarro, A. J. Burgasser, J. A. Caballero, J. M. Rees, D. Caselden, K. L. Cruz, R. Van Linge, D. J. Pinfield
arxiv-2004-04132.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by F. Marocco, R. L. Smart, E. E. Mamajek, L. M. Sarro, A. J. Burgasser, J. A. Caballero, J. M. Rees, D. Caselden, K. L. Cruz, R. Van Linge, D. J. Pinfield. We present ten new ultra-cool dwarfs in seven wide binary systems discovered using Gaia DR2 data, identified as part of our Gaia Ultra-Cool Dwarf Sample project.

arxiv-2104-08436.title: Deep Chaos Synchronization
arxiv-2104-08436.creator: Majid Mobini, Georges Kaddoum
arxiv-2104-08436.description: Abstract Abstract- In this study, we address the problem of chaotic synchronization over a noisy channel by introducing a novel Deep Chaos Synchronization (DCS) system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Conventional Deep Learning (DL) based communication strategies are extremely powerful but training on large data sets is usually a difficult and time-consuming procedure.

arxiv-2107-03184.title: Thermal noise competes with turbulent fluctuations below millimeter scales
arxiv-2107-03184.creator: Dmytro Bandak, Gregory L. Eyink, Alexei Mailybaev, Nigel Goldenfeld
arxiv-2107-03184.description: Abstract Turbulent flows frequently accompany physical, chemical and biological processes, such as mixing, two-phase flow, combustion and even foraging by bacteria and plankton larvae, all of which are in principle subject to thermal fluctuations already on scales of several microns.

arxiv-2111-09464.title: A Novel Grid-forming Voltage Control Strategy for Supplying Unbalanced Microgrid Loads Using Inverter-based Resources Thanks: This research is supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE) under the Solar EnergyTechnologies Office Award Number D
arxiv-2111-09464.creator: Bei Xu, Victor Paduani, Hui Yu, David Lubkeman, Ning Lu
arxiv-2111-09464.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel grid-forming voltage control strategy for a battery energy storage system to maintain balanced three-phase output voltages when serving unbalanced loads. A stationary reference frame ( α ​ β \alpha\beta ) based control scheme is proposed to regulate positive-sequence and negative-sequence voltages.

arxiv-2204-11644.title: Algorithms and Theory for Supervised Gradual Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2204-11644.creator: \name Jing Dong \email jingdong@link.cuhk.edu.cn
arxiv-2204-11644.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by \name Jing Dong \email jingdong@link.cuhk.edu.cn. The phenomenon of data distribution evolving over time has been observed in a range of applications, calling for the need for adaptive learning algorithms. We thus study the problem of supervised gradual domain adaptation, where labeled data from shifting distributions are available to the learner along the trajectory, and we aim to learn a classifier on a target data distribution of interest. Under this setting, we provide the first generalization upper bound on the learning error under mild assumptions.

arxiv-2208-02518.title: Fundamental Limitation on the Detectability of Entanglement
arxiv-2208-02518.creator: Pengyu Liu, Zhenhuan Liu, Shu Chen, Xiongfeng Ma
arxiv-2208-02518.description: Abstract Entanglement detection is essential in quantum information science and quantum many-body physics. It has been proved that entanglement exists almost surely for a random quantum state, while the realizations of effective entanglement criteria usually consume exponentially many resources with regard to system size or qubit number, and efficient criteria often perform poorly without prior knowledge.

arxiv-2402-03409.title: Where are the Teeth of the Fourth Power?
arxiv-2402-03409.creator: Lutz Stra ß \ss burger
arxiv-2402-03409.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Lutz Stra ß \ss burger. Our modern democracies are based on the separation of powers into legislative, executive, and judicial branches. In this setting, the mass media (such as the press, television, and radio) represents a fourth, virtual pillar, which, without legally anchored power, is intended to exercise a control function over the three state powers by means of truthful reporting and mediation of public opinion in order to prevent abuse of power.

arxiv-2406-07610.title: Regularizing infrared divergences in de Sitter spacetime: Loops, dimensional regularization, and cutoffs
arxiv-2406-07610.creator: Javier Huenupi, Ellie Hughes, Gonzalo A. Palma, Spyros Sypsas
arxiv-2406-07610.description: Abstract Correlation functions of light scalar fields in de Sitter spacetime, computed via standard perturbation theory, often exhibit secular growth characterized by time-dependent divergent terms in the form of powers of ln ⁡ a ⁡ ( t ) \ln a(t) , where a ⁡ ( t ) a(t) is the scale factor describing cosmic expansion.

arxiv-2407-21765.title: Engineering a multi-level bath for transmons with three-wave mixing and parametric drives
arxiv-2407-21765.creator: Xi Cao ∗,†, Maria Mucci ∗, Gangqiang Liu, David Pekker, Michael Hatridge ‡
arxiv-2407-21765.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Xi Cao ∗,†, Maria Mucci ∗, Gangqiang Liu, David Pekker, Michael Hatridge ‡. A quantum system with a tunable bath temperature provides an additional degree of freedom for quantum simulators. Such a system can be realized by parametrically modulating the coupling between the system and the bath. Here, by coupling a transmon qubit to a lossy Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) mode, we experimentally create a tunable bath for the qubit mode.

arxiv-2412-02944.title: Passive polarization-encoded BB84 protocol using a heralded single-photon source
arxiv-2412-02944.creator: Anju Rani, Vardaan Mongia, Parvatesh Parvatikar, Rutuj Gharate, Tanya Sharma, Jayanth Ramakrishnan, Pooja Chandravanshi, R. P. Singh
arxiv-2412-02944.description: Abstract The BB84 quantum key distribution protocol set the foundation for achieving secure quantum communication. Since its inception, significant advancements have aimed to overcome experimental challenges and enhance security. In this paper, we report the implementation of a passive polarization-encoded BB84 protocol using a heralded single-photon source.

arxiv-2502-08849.title: Geofeed Adoption and Authentication
arxiv-2502-08849.creator: Dipsy Desai, Kicho Yu, Sulyab Thottungal Valapu
arxiv-2502-08849.description: Abstract IP Geofeed is a recently proposed informational standard that allows network operators to publish the geographical location of deployed IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes. In this work we study the adoption of IP geofeed, assess deployment of geofeed at Regional Internet Registry and Autonomous System levels, and analyze adherence to RFC 8805 and RFC 9092 in deployed geofeeds.

arxiv-2505-00437.title: Quantum Corrected Geodesic Motion in Polymer Kerr-like Spacetime
arxiv-2505-00437.creator: Zhiyang Guo, Chen Lan, Yan Liu
arxiv-2505-00437.description: Abstract Rotating black holes are prevalent in astrophysical observations, and a Kerr-like solution that incorporates quantum gravity effects is essential for constructing realistic models. In this work, we analyze the geodesic motion of massive particles in a Kerr-like polymer spacetime, incorporating quantum corrections via a parameter A λ A_{\lambda} .

arxiv-2506-09907.creator: Francesco Bei and Simone Diverio and Stefano Trapani
arxiv-2506-09907.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Francesco Bei and Simone Diverio and Stefano Trapani. We introduce the notion of Kähler topologically hyperbolic manifold, as a “topological” generalization of Kähler [ Gro91 ] and weakly Kähler [ BDET24 ] hyperbolic manifolds. Analogously to [ BCDT24 ] , we show the birational invariance of this property and then that Kähler topologically hyperbolic manifolds are not uniruled nor bimeromorphic to compact Kähler manifolds with trivial first real Chern class.

arxiv-2601-13584.title: Nonlinear fractional-periodic boundary value problems with Hilfer fractional derivative: existence and numerical approximations of solutions Present address
arxiv-2601-13584.creator: Niels Goedegebure, Kateryna Marynets
arxiv-2601-13584.description: Abstract We prove conditions for existence of analytical solutions for boundary value problems with the Hilfer fractional derivative, generalizing the commonly used Riemann-Liouville and Caputo operators. The boundary values, referred to in this paper as fractional-periodic, are fractional integral conditions generalizing recurrent solution values for the non-Caputo case of the Hilfer fractional derivative.

pmc-10531179.title: Effects of Denture Treatment on Salivary Metabolites: A Pilot Study
pmc-10531179.creator: Narumi Ichigaya, Norishige Kawanishi, Takuya Adachi, Masahiro Sugimoto, Katsuhiko Kimoto, Noriyuki Hoshi, Barbara Manconi, Tiziana Cabras
pmc-10531179.description: Symptoms of oral discomfort such as dry mouth are common in older people wearing dentures. Such symptoms are mainly treated symptomatically. Many of these symptoms are related to saliva, and associations with salivary volume have been reported. Although denture treatment improves symptoms by increasing the amount of saliva, the effects on salivary components remain unclear.

pmc-11351178.title: Chemical and Structural Transformations of M–Al–CO3 Layered Double Hydroxides (M = Mg, Zn, or Co, M/Al = 2) at Elevated Temperatures: Quantitative Descriptions and Effect of Divalent Cations
pmc-11351178.creator: Kaito Matsuda, Ayaka Okuda, Nana Iio, Naoki Tarutani, Kiyofumi Katagiri, Kei Inumaru
pmc-11351178.description: Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) exhibit diverse chemical compositions and are being designed for promising applications such as CO2 adsorbents. Although many researchers have analyzed CO2 gas evolution and structural transformation behavior at elevated temperatures, there are still inconsistencies in results on the effect of different metal ions in LDHs.

pmc-11483712.title: Investigating Predictors of Decannulation Through Endoscopic Approach in Patients With Tracheostomy and Peristomal Subglottic Stenosis
pmc-11483712.creator: Nader Wehbi, David Ahmadian, Claire Gleadhill, Helena T Yip
pmc-11483712.description: ObjectivePeristomal subglottic stenosis (SGS) is a common sequela after tracheostomy, with severe cases precluding decannulation. Predictors of decannulation success in these patients following endoscopic intervention are not well studied. The aim of this study is to investigate predictors of successful decannulation and inform treatment decisions.

pmc-12563440.title: Digital Serious Games for Cancer Education and Behavioural Change: A Scoping Review of Evidence Across Patients, Professionals, and the Public
pmc-12563440.creator: Guangyan Si, Gillian Prue, Stephanie Craig, Tara Anderson, Gary Mitchell
pmc-12563440.description: Simple SummaryDigital serious games are being developed to support cancer education, prevention, care, and survivorship. However, their overall role and impact have not previously been synthesized in a single review. This scoping review examined serious games used across three stakeholder groups: the public, people living with cancer, and healthcare professionals.

pmc-12644604.title: Semantic orientation for indoor navigation system using large language models
pmc-12644604.creator: Marzena Halama, Sławomir Nowak, Konrad Połys
pmc-12644604.description: Autonomous robots play an important role in modern indoor navigation, but existing systems often struggle to achieve seamless human interaction and semantic understanding of environments. This paper presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven object recognition system enhanced by Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT-4 Vision and Gemini, to bridge this gap.

pmc-13317163.title: Tailoring acceptance and commitment therapy for parents of children with undiagnosed conditions: a qualitative pre-implementation study
pmc-13317163.creator: Sarah Rutzick, Sharon Aufox, Elizabeth Borto, Erika Lawrence, Kelli Scott, Rowan Forbes Shepherd, Carly Rasmussen, Jennifer L Young
pmc-13317163.description: BackgroundParents of undiagnosed children (POUC) experience significant psychosocial challenges, including anxiety, uncertainty, and isolation, that stem from parenting medically complex children while facing obstacles throughout the diagnostic journey. Despite these well-described challenges, a mental health intervention designed to meet the unique needs of POUC, which is necessary to promote the psychological and overall wellbeing of this population, does not exist.

pmc-13432866.title: HPV vaccination in the WHO South-East Asia Region: A scoping review of uptake, implementation challenges, and pathways to acceleration
pmc-13432866.creator: Siddhesh Kolambkar, Mansi Tomar, Nazneen Arif, Showket Hussain, Ekta Gupta, Shalini Singh
pmc-13432866.description: Cervical cancer remains a major public health concern in the WHO South-East Asia Region (SEAR), where human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage remains uneven. This scoping review synthesizes evidence on HPV vaccine uptake and implementation strategies and challenges across SEAR countries.
